title: Acceleration expression
description: Essential: Student states the correct acceleration magnitude as a = eE/m, derived from Newton's second law and the force on an electron in an electric field.

title: Maximum distance formula
description: Essential: Student provides the correct expression for the maximum penetration distance, x_max = m v_0^2 / (2eE), using work-energy or kinematics.

title: Kinetic energy at half distance
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the kinetic energy at x_max/2 as (1/4) m v_0^2.

title: Correct force direction
description: Important: Student recognizes the force (and thus acceleration) opposes the initial velocity because the electron's charge is negative.

title: Work-energy application
description: Important: Student applies the work-energy theorem correctly, relating change in kinetic energy to work done by the electric force.

title: Sign error in force
description: Pitfall: Student uses a = -eE/m but treats it as a positive magnitude in subsequent motion equations without justification, or incorrectly uses a positive sign for acceleration.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: Student explicitly checks or states the units for distance and energy are consistent (meters and joules).

title: Alternative kinematic derivation
description: Optional: Student uses constant-acceleration kinematics (v^2 = v_0^2 + 2a x) to find the maximum distance.
